confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches. One was the RBA lookup and two were price lookups. The price results were aggregated cost-of-living figures (Numbeo-derived data via Expatica and Idealista, plus PortugalBuyersAgent and MyLifeElsewhere) and a travel guide. They gave beer about €2.50-3.13, cappuccino about €1.62-1.81, an inexpensive meal about €12.5, and a mid-range meal for two about €35-40. These were converted to USD at roughly 1.18 USD per EUR, an approximation based on a EUR/USD figure quoted in the results and not an RBA rate. Cocktail (€5-12, central about €8) and wine (€2.50-6, central about €4-4.5) came from less reliable guide and listing ranges. Both are consistent with the local beer price. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for July peak season in the Algarve. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings, so these are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Faro is an Algarve city that runs slightly above the Portuguese average (MyLifeElsewhere puts it about 8% higher overall). I compared it with other Algarve tourist towns such as Lagos and Portimão, and with mid-sized southern European tourist cities. Summer demand is high, but it is less expensive than Lisbon or Porto in peak season.
